context: Workflow is intended to summarize the top trending public repo, but tool surface is unrestricted. Combined with indirect prompt injection from trending HTML/README content and an over-scoped PAT, private README text can be pulled into the agent and demo UI.
evidence: get_github_repository_readme_agent_action uses repo_name = input.replace('https://github.com/', '') then Github(auth=Token).get_repo(repo_name).get_readme(). Handler passes parameters[name=repo].value without format or ownership checks. OpenAPI schema marks repo as free-form string.
summary: Bedrock agent GitHub action Lambda accepts an arbitrary repo parameter, strips only a https://github.com/ prefix, and uses a Secrets Manager PAT to fetch that repository README with no allowlist to trending/public repos.

validation.confidence_rationale: Code clearly accepts arbitrary repo parameters and uses a PAT for get_readme with no allowlist; only uncertainty is operator PAT scope and reliability of prompt-injection steering.
rubric: Tool input attacker/model influenced: yes
Authorization/allowlist missing: yes
Secret-backed API called: yes
Data returns to user-visible summary: yes
Impact depends on PAT scope: yes (precondition)
validation.evidence: get_github_repository_readme_agent_action strips only https://github.com/ prefix and calls get_repo().get_readme() with Secrets Manager token. Handler passes repo query parameter unsanitized.
validation.counterevidence_or_proof_gap: Demo workflow prompts aim at trending public repos; exploitation of private data needs a PAT that can read private repos and successful agent tool steering (prompt injection).
validation.remaining_uncertainty: Operator-chosen PAT scopes are not in repo; treat broad PAT as realistic misconfiguration the code fails to constrain.
validation.source: Bedrock agent tool parameter repo (model/tool-chosen; influenceable via tool-visible content)
validation.control: missing allowlist; no validation that repo is the selected trending public repository
validation.preconditions: MostPopularRepo Bedrock Agents workflow invoked; PAT has access to sensitive repos.

attack_path.dataflow: Workflow invokes Bedrock agent -> agent calls GitHubAPIs /get_github_repository_readme with attacker/model-chosen repo -> PAT-authenticated get_readme -> contents returned to agent/UI summary
attack_path.reachability: Any principal that can start PromptChainDemo-MostPopularRepoBedrockAgents (webapp users). Steering may use indirect prompt injection via trending page/README content.
attack_path.counterevidence: Intended use is public trending repos; private impact requires over-scoped PAT. No user-supplied repo field in UI, so direct parameter injection is model/tool mediated.
attack_path.severity_rationale: Missing tool allowlist is a real broken control. Severity medium because confidential impact depends on PAT scope and successful agent steering, which is realistic for agent systems but not guaranteed.
attack_path.change_conditions: Raise to high if the documented/default token is expected to access private org repos or if a reliable tool-force path is demonstrated. Lower if tool enforces an allowlist of the single selected public trending repo.

context: Independent of SSTI: even if template evaluation were disabled, resource fetches during PDF render remain. Lambda has internet egress by default (no VPC isolation in stack).
evidence: md2pdf converts markdown to HTML then HTML(string=..., base_url=cwd).write_pdf(). WeasyPrint URLFetcher/default_url_fetcher performs network and protocol fetches for linked resources. User-controlled location and model-produced itinerary can introduce Markdown image/link syntax that becomes fetchable URLs.
summary: The same PDF generation path converts untrusted markdown to HTML and renders it with WeasyPrint, whose default URL fetcher retrieves remote http(s) and file resources referenced by the document (images, stylesheets, etc.), enabling SSRF or local file disclosure from the Lambda environment.

validation.method: static source trace + dependency URL fetcher review
validation.confidence_rationale: Untrusted markdown is converted to HTML and rendered with WeasyPrint, whose default URLFetcher retrieves http(s)/file resources. User location and model itinerary both land in the markdown document.
rubric: Attacker or model content reaches document renderer: yes
Renderer fetches URLs by default: yes (WeasyPrint URLFetcher)
No allowlist/deny for schemes/hosts: yes
Network identity useful: yes (Lambda default egress)
Distinct from SSTI impact: yes (SSRF/file fetch even without template RCE)
validation.evidence: md2pdf uses markdown() then HTML(string=raw_html, base_url=cwd).write_pdf(). Weasyprint urls.py default_url_fetcher/URLFetcher.fetch performs outbound retrieval. Markdown image syntax and HTML resources become fetch targets.
validation.counterevidence_or_proof_gap: Did not run WeasyPrint in this environment to capture a live fetch log. Library default behavior is documented in its URL fetcher implementation.
validation.remaining_uncertainty: Whether specific Markdown extensions emit raw HTML img tags vs only markdown images; both are sufficient for URL introduction via common markdown image syntax.
validation.source: location and itinerary strings in PDF markdown
validation.control: no custom url_fetcher, scheme allowlist, or HTML sanitization
validation.preconditions: Same as trip planner execution path.

attack_path.dataflow: User/model content in PDF markdown -> HTML conversion -> WeasyPrint fetches linked http(s)/file URLs using Lambda network identity
attack_path.reachability: Same authenticated trip planner path. Markdown image/link syntax is sufficient.
attack_path.counterevidence: Lambda not in a VPC with rich internal peers; impact may be limited to cloud metadata (IMDSv2 may mitigate), attacker-controlled callback, or reachable internal HTTP depending on account networking.

attack_path.change_conditions: Raise if PDF Lambda can reach sensitive internal services or if file:// yields secret material. Lower if a restrictive custom URLFetcher deny-by-default is installed.

context: Application does not expose arbitrary ARN input in UI fields, so exploitation needs UI compromise, SSRF to IMDS, or malicious code in the container. Shared-role multi-user design.

context: Requires ability to start PromptChainDemo-TripPlanner (authenticated Streamlit user in deployed webapp, or any principal that can StartExecution). Impact is RCE in the PDF Lambda role (S3 put/get on itinerary bucket plus Lambda runtime credentials).
evidence: pdf_creator builds itinerary_content with f-string interpolation of event['location'] and event['itinerary'], then calls md2pdf(..., raw=itinerary_content). md2pdf 3.1.1 always executes jinja2.Template(raw).render(context) on that string. Jinja2 default templates expose builtins (confirmed locally via Template(...).render()). Location is taken directly from $$.Execution.Input.location in the state machine payload, which originates from the Streamlit text_input.
summary: Trip planner PDF Lambda embeds attacker-controlled location (and model itinerary) into a markdown string passed to md2pdf(), which Jinja2-renders the raw markdown before converting it to HTML/PDF. Unsandboxed Jinja evaluation enables server-side template injection and code execution inside the Lambda.

validation.method: static source trace + library behavior confirmation
validation.confidence_rationale: Direct dataflow from Streamlit location input to Execution.Input.location into f-string markdown passed to md2pdf; md2pdf 3.1.1 source unconditionally runs jinja2.Template(raw).render(); local Jinja2 renders attacker expressions and exposes builtins.
rubric: Attacker-controlled source identified: yes (location text_input)
Sink reaches code execution primitive: yes (unsandboxed Jinja2)
Control missing/bypassable: yes (no sanitization/escaping before md2pdf)
Reachable from in-scope surface: yes (authenticated trip planner demo)
Impact security-relevant: yes (RCE in Lambda)
validation.evidence: pdf_creator/index.py interpolates location/itinerary into raw markdown and calls md2pdf. Extracted md2pdf/core.py shows Template(raw).render(context) before markdown/WeasyPrint. Jinja2 Template('{{7*7}}').render() => '49'; Template accessing self.__init__.__globals__.__builtins__ returns builtins including eval/exec/open.
validation.counterevidence_or_proof_gap: Full Lambda+WeasyPrint runtime PoC not executed in this environment (native deps). SSTI occurs at Jinja stage before PDF write, so WeasyPrint is not required for code execution.
validation.remaining_uncertainty: Exact post-exploitation IAM blast radius depends on the generated PDF Lambda role (S3 itinerary bucket access confirmed in stack; no broader managed policies in source).
validation.control: none on location before PDF; no Jinja sandbox or non-template markdown renderer
validation.preconditions: Principal can start PromptChainDemo-TripPlanner (Cognito-authenticated webapp user or equivalent StartExecution IAM).

attack_path.dataflow: Cognito user enters location in Trip Planner -> Streamlit start_execution(PromptChainDemo-TripPlanner, {location}) -> Step Functions passes $$.Execution.Input.location to PDF Lambda -> f-string markdown -> md2pdf Jinja2 Template.render -> attacker code runs in Lambda
attack_path.reachability: Authenticated demo user (or any caller of the state machine). No special admin role required beyond normal webapp use.
attack_path.counterevidence: Cognito gate prevents anonymous internet abuse when deployed as designed; still fully reachable to every legitimate demo user.
attack_path.severity_rationale: Authenticated users get server-side template injection leading to code execution in the PDF Lambda. Not critical because Cognito authentication is required and the Lambda IAM is relatively narrow (S3 itinerary), but RCE on a production demo path is high.
attack_path.change_conditions: Raise to critical if the webapp is exposed without Cognito or the Lambda role gains broad account privileges. Lower to medium only if md2pdf is replaced/configured to never Jinja-render untrusted strings and that control is verified.
